  • With 250+ client engagements across both agency and embedded in-house roles, Vitalii Khomenko has seen product teams from the inside in a way few designers have.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

With 250+ client engagements across both agency and embedded in-house roles, Vitalii Khomenko has seen product teams from the inside in a way few designers have. Here he makes the case for a newly introduced kind of design workflow built for the AI era, and explains why the window to adapt is narrower than most founders think.

For the last decade, every startup conversation about speed eventually became a conversation about engineering. Hiring more developers, cutting scope, choosing a simpler stack, it was almost always a dev-side problem. Vitalii Khomenko, Principal Designer at Orizon Design and founder of Fluente LLC, argues that's no longer true. And he has a specific view on what teams should do instead.

Industry observers note that what makes Khomenko's perspective worth taking seriously isn't just seniority. It's the specific shape of his experience. Over a career spanning 250+ client engagements, he has worked both as an external specialist brought in to deliver and as an embedded designer who became the single connective thread between product, brand, and execution. That dual vantage point is rare. Most designers live on one side of that line. Khomenko has operated extensively on both, which gives him an unusually clear read on where friction actually originates inside product teams, and where it doesn't.

Industry observers note that his work spans early-stage startups finding their first visual language and established brands managing complex, multi-disciplinary design systems. Across that range, certain patterns repeat. And the pattern that started becoming impossible to ignore this year pointed him toward a conclusion that is reshaping how he thinks a modern design workflow should actually be structured.

In a recent development, the bottleneck didn't disappear. It moved. And the workflow needs to move with it.

When shipping code was slow, the existing design workflow made sense. Multiple rounds of revision, user testing, iteration, all of that fit naturally into the window while engineering caught up. That window is now gone, and most design workflows were never updated to reflect it.

In a recent development, "Founders are asking design teams to move at the same speed as an AI-assisted dev pipeline, and design doesn't compress the same way code does," Khomenko claims. The result is a workflow that was built around a constraint that no longer exists, applied to a pipeline that has fundamentally changed around it.

Industry observers note that the forced choice between polish and speed that product teams are now navigating isn't upcoming as a concept. What's new is how stark it has become, and how directly it traces back to a workflow problem rather than a people problem. "Because development is cheap and fast now, there's constant pressure to ship the next thing immediately," he explains. "But the products that actually retain customers are still the ones where the details were considered carefully. Fewer revision rounds isn't a process improvement if it means shipping avoidable friction.".

Recent findings suggest that khomenko has watched this play out across enough teams, at enough stages, to be specific about where the existing workflow breaks down. The matter isn't design judgment. It's where that judgment sits in the process, and what format it's expected to produce at the end.

To understand Khomenko's proposed fix, it helps to understand exactly where the current workflow stalls. For most product teams, the end of the design process looks like this: a designer produces polished, dev-ready screens inside Figma, and hands that file to engineering. Engineering then interprets those screens, translates the visual decisions into code, and builds from there.

That translation step, Figma file to working code, is where the pipeline now breaks down. AI-assisted engineering has made the building part dramatically faster. But the translation step hasn't changed. An engineer still has to read a Figma file, interpret spacing, extract assets, make judgment calls about component structure, and write the implementation from scratch. That process takes the same amount of time it always did.

According to recent reports, "The manual workflow inside Figma simply isn't keeping up with AI-boosted engineering," Khomenko indicates. "The design handoff is quietly becoming the thing everyone is waiting on.".

Industry observers note that the result is a pipeline where everything around the handoff has accelerated, and the handoff itself has become the single point of drag. Figma, in other words, was built for a world where engineering was the slow part. It wasn't designed to feed a pipeline where engineering moves at AI speed.

This is the core of what Khomenko is proposing, and it's a more significant structural shift than it might first appear.

It has been revealed that in his workflow, Figma doesn't disappear. It moves. Rather than serving as both the exploration environment and the final delivery artifact, Figma becomes the visual exploration layer exclusively: the place where brand identity is established, layout logic is worked through, and design direction is validated. It remains the right tool for figuring out what something should look and feel like.

Sources indicate that but the final delivery, the artifact that actually goes to engineering, is code. Specifically, components built into prepared libraries that engineering can work from and scale directly, without any translation step in between.

The difference in implementation speed is the point. When a designer delivers a coded component library rather than a Figma file, engineering doesn't need to interpret anything. The decisions are already expressed in the language they're building in. What previously required an engineer to read, interpret, and re-create from a visual reference now arrives ready to use. In a pipeline running on AI-assisted development, that difference compounds fast.

"Figma is still the right place to explore what something should look and feel like," Khomenko says. "But handing over a Figma file and asking engineering to implement it is now the slow path. Delivering in code is the fast path. That's the shift.".

In a recent development, executing this workflow requires a different kind of designer, and Khomenko is direct about that. The UI/UX designer becoming a Design Engineer is, in his assessment, not a distant possibility. It is a matter of time, and the teams treating it as a future consideration rather than a present reality are the ones most likely to find themselves stuck at the handoff.

But Khomenko is equally clear about what this shift doesn't mean. Delivering in code is one part of the role, not the whole of it. The full design cycle isn't going anywhere. Applying branding to imagery, producing animations, building marketing materials, these remain essential creative tasks that require a broad and varied toolkit well beyond code. "The designer of the near future isn't just generating code," he says. "They're moving across the full cycle, brand, motion, marketing, product, with design engineering as an notable and growing part of that stack, not a replacement for it.".

In a recent development, what changes is that code-ready delivery becomes a core expectation within that stack. The designer who can move fluidly from visual exploration in Figma to component delivery in code, while also carrying the brand thinking, motion, and marketing creativity that differentiates products at the surface level consumers actually experience, is the profile that the new workflow demands.

In a recent development, khomenko is candid that no single version of this workflow has fully standardized yet. Every team is figuring it out differently. The tools are evolving, the handoff expectations are shifting, and the processes teams are building around all of it vary considerably. There is no off-the-shelf playbook.

But this is precisely where his 250+ engagements become more than a credential. They're a dataset. Having watched enough teams, at enough stages, through enough cycles of tooling change, Khomenko can see through the noise of individual variation and identify what's directionally true even when the specifics are still in flux. "Each team's workflow is really custom at this stage," he states. "But some general patterns of how this is going to look in the near future are already visible.".

Sources indicate that those patterns consistently point in the same direction: design judgment moving earlier, final delivery moving into code, and the designer's role expanding in technical range while staying broad in creative scope. The exact tools and sequences will keep shifting. The underlying logic of the workflow Khomenko is describing is already taking shape in the teams paying closest attention.

For founders and product leads, the workflow Khomenko is describing has direct implications for how teams are staffed, budgeted, and structured.

Front-load design judgment. The biggest leverage in the new workflow isn't faster execution, it's better problem definition before generation starts. Bring senior design thinking in earlier, when it can shape what gets built rather than polish what's already done.

Sources indicate that separate exploration from delivery. Figma and the visual exploration phase serve a distinct purpose from the final delivery layer. Treat them as separate stages with separate expectations, rather than collapsing them into a single step expected to produce everything.

Shift the delivery expectation to code. Whether that means hiring for Design Engineer range, developing it internally, or restructuring handoffs, the end of the design pipeline needs to arrive in a form engineering can work from directly. The translation step is where time goes to die, and it's now the most avoidable part of the process.

Protect the full creative stack. Design engineering matters more than it ever has. It is not, however, the whole job. Teams that reduce design to code generation will lose the brand thinking, motion, and marketing creativity that differentiates products at the surface level consumers actually experience.

Stay flexible. The workflow is still forming. Teams that build rigidity into their process now will find themselves redoing that work within a year. The teams getting this right are the ones building enough adaptability into their structures to absorb what's still coming.

"The Figma handoff made sense when engineering was the slow part," Khomenko says. "Engineering isn't the slow part anymore. Delivering in code isn't the future of design workflow. For the teams paying attention, it's already the present.".

Industry News: Grand Theft Auto 6 launch day - all the news and rection as GTA 6 arrived around the world

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3460 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide.
  • Sources indicate that have you played it yet?
  • It has been revealed that more broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide. It's destined to become the largest video game release of all time, and probably one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time. So we're doing a launch day live blog to chart its arrival in the world.

Sources indicate that have you played it yet? I'm curious how many people stayed up until midnight in their region to give the game a go. I couldn't manage it but my college-age son was contemplating it. And if you have played it, what do you think - what are your early impressions? Is this what you were waiting for?

It has been revealed that more broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world. I've already seen nearly all mainstream news and media outlets attempt to cover the game - and many other kinds of businesses - so will GTA 6 make people reappraise video games?

According to recent reports, moreover, exactly how big will the launch be? The record books are ready to be written in, but what exactly will be written? And how will other games fare in GTA's wake - better, or worse? There's lots to consider as the ripples spread around the world.

We'll pull-in stories and developments, and your comments, as we chart the arrival of Rockstar's game around the world. Let's get to it.

Our live coverage of this event has finished.

According to recent reports, an historic day in gaming and there's loads to unpack. But to begin with, this: did you take a day off to play GTA 6, and have you played it yet?

Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

The marketing push by Rockstar to have GTA 6 imprint on real-world cities has been impressive to see. There have been festivals in Miami, Selfridges dedicated a portion of its department store to selling GTA merch, but there's more than this besides. The London Standard summarised much of the activity in London in a video on Instagram.

A post shared by The Standard (@thelondonstandard).

Rockstar employment tribunal verdict could take weeks.

Industry observers note that the din of release is in danger of drowning out the Rockstar employment tribunal that came to a close this week in Scotland. Former Eurogamer video producer Chris Bratt - now co-owner of People Make Games - has been following the case closely, and reported yesterday that a verdict in the case could take "weeks".

Industry observers note that he quotes Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as swiftly as I possibly can.".

Sources indicate that and that's it for the Rockstar tribunal! We await the judge's decision, but how long will it take? Judge Lucy Wiseman: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

Yesterday, we independently confirmed that most, if not all, of the fired Rockstar employees are credited in the GTA 6 credits - which are, according to Chris Tapsell, our reviewer, an enormous thing in their own right.

Here’s how significant it is, news-wise:.

Yesterday, my mother _(whose single dabble in gaming over the years can be described as,“working out the way to bypass the Brontosaurus Guarding Causeway in the text adventure Time Machine, is to GIVE it the Ship’s Biscuit found aboard the Marie Celeste”)_ texted me to ask if I was “ready for tomorrow?”.

I instantly assumed I’d made or hinted at some plan to do something with her and subsequently forgotten.

Recent findings suggest that BUT, NO. She was asking if I was ready for GTA. A product I have never mentioned in her presence in all my many years.

So if you’ve got the over-seventies non-gamers talking… I’d say you’ve cracked it.

Goodness! And will your mother also be playing it?

My inbox is flooded with all kinds of brands trying to get in on the GTA 6 hype.

Industry observers note that the most recent one? Petrol prices. "Having to refuel your car in GTA 6 adds another layer of realism to the game, but it's something real-life drivers have to think about every time they get behind the wheel," noted Beth Fountain, fuel expert at somewhere called Interfuels.

"With petrol and diesel prices remaining high, filling up can take a significant chunk out of someone's monthly budget, particularly for those who rely on their vehicles for work or regular travel.

"While players might find the new mechanic frustrating, it's a reminder of how much we depend on fuel in everyday life and how rapidly those costs can add up.".

There's another one from Just Eat, the food delivery tech giant, which has apparently made a real controller with Just Eat order button on it for you to order food while gaming. It's not specifically GTA 6-linked but it's jumping on that bandwagon. The controller is apparently synced to your Just Eat account. Imagine mashing that by accident and having an accidental feast turn up.

"When you're deep into a high-stakes gaming session nothing kills the moment faster than having to pause the action just to sort out food. With the Just ChEAT Button, Just Eat has unlocked the ultimate hack to evade the kitchen, enabling gamers to stay just where they are and locked into play," said Just East UK and Ireland marketing director Tina Koehler.

Sources indicate that it's not clear where you can buy this controller or how much it costs. It's described as "limited edition". I wonder if that means only one has been made.

The goofy things people are already doing in GTA 6.

Many people are playing GTA 6 already of course and doing expectedly bizarre things in it. From lobbing hammers like Crocodile Dundee lobs cans of tinned food, to dropkicking people, to attempting to dive through a car window while oiled up and in one's pants - Connor has rounded up some of the goofiest clips around.

You are brilliant, Eurogamer readers!

I just want to resurface the winning entry to the GTA memories competition we ran at the tail-end of last week, because it's funny and uplifting, and I still smile about it.

My favourite GTA memory is introducing my nan to Vice City.

She'd never played a video game before, so I told her she could pretty much do whatever she wanted.

She spent the first 20 minutes driving around obeying traffic lights and apologising whenever she bumped into another car.

Then she accidentally punched someone.

I don't know what happened, but something just clicked.

Within half an hour she'd stolen a police car, run over several pedestrians and was shouting at the telly because the police wouldn’t leave her alone.

My grandad came in to see what all the noise was about.

In a recent development, without even looking up she just noted, "I'm wanted for murder, Barry. Put the kettle on.".

Genuinely one of the funniest afternoons of my childhood.

In a recent development, I'm on the management team for a charity and they've scheduled their AGM for tonight at 6pm. Of all the dates! I've had to weigh up not doing my duty for selfish video game reasons.

According to recent reports, I must be growing up because I've decided that going to the AGM is the right thing to do and that GTA 6 probably isn't that good, anyway. Right?

Recent findings suggest that well! Allow the Eurogamer comments to decide. I think you should set GTA 6 up in another room in the building you're holding the AGM in, and find excuses during it to nip out and play. It'll be like a Mrs Doubtfire moment. Nothing can go wrong.

Industry observers note that another email from a shopping comparison site, Idealo, and this time about PS5 Pro demand, which has apparently leapt by 57 percent week on week because of GTA 6. This, by the way, is exactly what the industry was hoping would happen - that GTA 6 would reinvigorate console sales, which were slumping, not least because of their unprecedented rising prices. Apparently the price of PS5 consoles is rising in step with this demand.

"Grand Theft Auto releases are major cultural moments, and GTA 6 is already having a noticeable impact on the wider gaming market, particularly when it comes to console demand," Katy Phillips from Idealo noted.

Industry observers note that "We're seeing a significant increase in interest in the PS5 Pro, with demand jumping by 57 percent in the week leading up to launch. At the same time, the price of the console has climbed by more than £450 since the end of October.".

GTA 6 videos you might find helpful.

IGN has produced a bunch of good Grand Theft Auto 6 videos I'm surfacing here in case you've missed them. There are a few performance-related videos of the game running on PlayStation and Xbox hardware:.

There's also footage of the first 15 minutes of the first mission:.

And some scuba diving and treasure hunting:.

GTA 6 is Metacritic's highest rated game ever.

Industry observers note that A notable moment yesterday was GTA 6 being crowned as the highest-rated game ever on review-averaging site Metacritic. The game right now holds a 99 score there, averaged from 156 critics' reviews. The previous champion was the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, from 1998, with the same 99 average critics score. Will it retain the title as the days and weeks unfold?

In a recent development, chris' expansive GTA 6 review is of course one of those contributing to that score. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

More ridiculous GTA 6 launch piggybacking and this time it's an email with a therapist talking about how the game might help teens with their dating outlooks.

States Natalie Buchwald, therapist and founder of Manhattan Mental Health Counseling:.

Recent findings suggest that "Psychologists sometimes talk about 'relationship scripts': the unspoken expectations we absorb about how relationships work, what partners owe each other and what success looks like. We pick these up long before we have much experience of our own, from family, friends, online spaces and the stories we see in entertainment.

It has been revealed that "No single film, game or influencer shapes someone's values on its own. What matters more is the overall mix of messages a person encounters, and whether they have the space to question them. That's particularly relevant now that dating advice is so widely available online, where some content frames relationships around status, control or getting something in return, rather than mutual respect.

"That's why the most useful thing parents can do isn't to hand over a set of rules. It's to help young people think critically about the scripts they're picking up. Being curious rather than critical, and asking what they've seen, what they think of it and what they believe makes a good partner, tends to keep conversations open.

Industry observers note that "Entertainment can play a helpful role here. A story built around a partnership, like Jason and Lucia's, can give parents a natural, low pressure starting point for conversations that might otherwise feel awkward.".

In a recent development, chris referenced some of this in his review, praising Jason's tender and caring side, and his not being a toxic asshole. GTA 6 is also the first game to not only feature a couple but a female playable lead, having very much revolved around male fantasies in the past.

You can't use cheat in GTA 6 until you finish the main story.

A reminder that cheats aren't usable in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you've finished the main story. Chris confirmed this yesterday, and offered details about cheats do work in the game when you've unlocked them.

More brand opportunism, this time optician Specsavers, and at least this one has a novel approach: a spoof partnership with a GTA tech giant that has nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto.

Specsavers is circulating a very budget-looking partnership with a trucking firm called GTA Transport. It's billed as a "mix-up" in an email, but it's all far too staged and knowing to really be one.

Recent findings suggest that "It might not be the GTA partnership I originally had in mind but a deal's a deal," said Specsavers marketing person Neil Liddle. "I'm pleased to offer every driver at GTA Transport a free eye test.".

Industry observers note that bugz Singh at GTA Transport noted: "We were surprised when Specsavers got in touch, but we're delighted to be the GTA they've teamed up with. Our drivers spend all day on the road, so they're looking forward to their eye tests.".

It has been revealed that the visuals are just something else. Even at this early stage, the story has already got me interested and invested in Jason and Lucia. And to top it all off, when I first started messing around with the car radio, ‘Master of Puppets’ was playing.

The second thing is that like all gtas is serves a reminder of what a hellscape urban America is. I’ve never been to the keys, but what looks like it should be a lovely set of islands is of course mostly a massive highway.

...long story short, what was intended to be a 1 hour go on a school night ended up being 3 hours and I slept through my alarm and am working from home today! I'll be playing this and pretty much only this for the next month or 2, no doubt...haven't been gripped by a game since Clair Obscure...nice to have that feeling back!

Some nice accounts of playing the game so far. Keep 'em coming!

GTA 6 developers fear for their jobs now the game has shipped.

Industry observers note that rockstar and Take-Two stand to make billions of dollars from GTA 6, but there's an enormous workforce - 4,711 people at last count - working at the GTA studio. Will they keep their jobs now the game has come out? That staff-count more than doubled after Red Dead Redemption 2 was released but will it grow again now?

Fears of lay-offs reach top volume both as the game is released and as Rockstar workers vote wheter to formally recognise a workers union there - a union that's proved so problematic in the past. Sherif has the full story below.

GameStop boss slams 'code in a box' trend in wake of GTA 6's discless release.

Recent findings suggest that the boss of game-related retailer GameStop has spoken out about the trend of 'code in a box' game releases. This, of course, is pertinent this week with the discless release of GTA 6.

In a recent development, "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," GameStop boss Ryan Cohen told Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop." Dom has the full story:.

Industry observers note that I have always wondered if one of the reasons I bounced off 5 was that I got it a long while down the line. (Also... I really didn't like the main characters).

Decided to be part of this "global media event" and bought it last night.

The intro is pretty gripping story wise, with a decent twist that somehow was kept completely under wraps.

Driving takes some getting used to, but the use of adaptive triggers on PS5 is great for this making cruising fairly easy. The traffic density and “smaller” roads really make getting about the city nicely realistically annoying. Spending more time cruising than normal for a GTA.

Being quoted is the risk one runs!

The spoof websites aren't in GTA 6 because Rockstar didn't think they were "necessary".

In a recent development, the spoof websites of previous GTA games don't make it into GTA 6. Apparently Rockstar didn't deem them "necessary". Let me tell you, as someone who writes for a website, that cuts deep.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector has strong words for Rockstar about GTA 6.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector, who was also involved in the making of influential series like Thief, System Shock and Ultima Underworld, has a few strong words to say about GTA 6. Or rather not GTA 6 itself but the colossal workforce, budget and development time Rockstar had to make i with.

"A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries," Spector said. "Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

I'm genuinely surprised that some gaming companies are ernestly trying to release and market their games today of all days - even this week. Did you want to know about a Goat Simulator 3 expansion that arrived today, called Dizzyworld? Well, now you do. And it's by far the only game I'm being sent press releases about.

My favourite press release about a game unrelated to GTA 6 - though it sounds like a parody that could be in the game - is one that made me do a double-take. "Sperm Adventure 'Become' Delayed to First Half of 2027," it read. The entire press release is packed with innuendo. And it's - judging by its Steam page - a real thing. Will you "embark on life's greatest tiny journey"?

GTA 6 is dominating Twitch viewer figures in a major way.

Back to GTA 6, and the impact of this game's arrival can be seen clearly on Twitch viewership numbers at the moment. GTA 6 is by far the most watched category on the streaming platform, with more than 1.6 million viewers. The next highest category is the broad "just chatting" category 2ith 330k viewers, followed by World of Warcraft with 72k viewers.

For balance, presentation and intro to story/characters are great.

"Laser Disc vibes" is not a phrase I've heard before, but I like it and think I'll steal it.

All 34 of the fired Rockstar employees are in the GTA 6 credits.

Sources indicate that here's a curious development. With Rockstar publishing the full cast list for GTA 6, I've been more able to cross-check the names of the 34 fired employees against it. And, success, they do all appear in the credits. But six of them are not contained in the "former employees" section of the credits, where everyone else is, which is curious. I'm trying to find out what gives.

Jason Duval actor finally confirmed.

Incidentally, that full cast list also confirms - finally - who the actor is that plays Jason Duval in the game. And, yes, it's Dylan Rourke, who everyone thought it was.

More than 2 million people used Fresh Zealand trick to play GTA 6 early.

I tried doing the Newly introduced Zealand trick on my PS5 yesterday evening - I'd spent the entire afternoon convinced it would be a doddle to play GTA 6 early doing so. It wasn't. So I played Galactic Racers instead (which is great).

Nevertheless, millions of people did use the Latest Zealand time-zone trick to play the game early - more than 2 million people, in fact, which is more than a third of the population of the country.

You can make GTA 6 easier by altering two key settings.

Recent findings suggest that as people start playing the game, issues of difficulty come up, and altering the game to your preference. And as Dom reported, there are two very key changes you can make to the game - in lieu of difficulty settings - to change how challenging it is to play.

How are you all doing? It's nearly the end of the day - are you excited about getting home to play the game? Are you nonplussed? Are you perhaps playing the game already? Temperature check! As they say.

It has been revealed that the UK working day is coming to an end here. Thanks everyone for popping in and good luck exploring the game tonight, if you are. That's a wrap on our rolling coverage for today, though our general news coverage continues into the evening.

Tech Report: Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that tiny magnetic structures called skyrmions could help pave the way for a newly introduced generation of computers that process information more like the human brain while using far less electricity.
  • In a recent development, A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides fresh insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them.
  • Most of the research was conducted at the Institute of Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany, with contributions from a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tiny magnetic structures called skyrmions could help pave the way for a newly introduced generation of computers that process information more like the human brain while using far less electricity. Although most people have never heard of skyrmions, these microscopic magnetic vortices may eventually play an vital role in how computers store and process data.

In a recent development, A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides fresh insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them. The findings could help researchers develop smaller, more efficient computing systems and advance emerging quantum technologies.

Most of the research was conducted at the Institute of Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany, with contributions from a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).

"Skyrmions are small, magnetic vortices that can store information in a completely new way," explained Asle Sudbø, who leads NTNU's Centre for Quantum Spintronics (QuSpin).

Unlike conventional technologies, which require increasing amounts of space and energy to handle growing quantities of data, skyrmions could offer a much more efficient alternative.

"Instead of the current technology, where we constantly need more space and energy to process data, skyrmions could make it possible to build much smaller and more energy-efficient data storage systems," explained Sudbø.

Tiny Magnetic Vortices Could Enable Brain-Like Computers.

The potential applications of skyrmions extend well beyond conventional data storage. They are also notable to spintronics, which explores ways to use the magnetic properties of electrons in electronic devices, and to research involving topological quantum effects.

One particularly promising possibility is the development of computers that operate in ways similar to biological brains.

"These nanoscale vortices could help develop computers that resemble biological brains," noted Sudbø.

It has been revealed that rather than relying on conventional transistor-based computing, such systems could use magnetism to process information. In principle, this approach could dramatically reduce electricity consumption, potentially allowing future computers to perform complex tasks with very little energy.

Turning that possibility into practical technology, however, requires scientists to understand exactly how skyrmions behave and how to manipulate them reliably.

The latest research represents an important advance toward that goal.

Scientists Film Magnetic Skyrmion Lattices Melting for the First Time.

Sources indicate that skyrmions do not always exist as isolated magnetic structures. Under certain conditions, they organize themselves into repeating patterns known as lattices, resembling the orderly arrangement of atoms in a crystal, but on a much smaller scale.

Scientists can manipulate these arrangements, a capability that could be essential for using skyrmions in future computing devices.

In the new study, researchers achieved something that had not been demonstrated before. They recorded the melting of a magnetic skyrmion lattice as it happened while simultaneously controlling individual skyrmions.

"For the first time, researchers have managed to film how a magnetic skyrmion lattice melts in real time, while simultaneously being able to manipulate each individual skyrmion directly as they film it. For example, both their shape and size can be changed 'on the fly'," noted Sudbø.

In a recent development, the ability to observe this process directly provides a clearer picture of how skyrmions respond when their organized structures break apart. It also allows researchers to study how changing the size and shape of individual magnetic vortices affects their behavior.

A Fresh Step Toward Energy-Efficient Computing.

It has been revealed that understanding how skyrmions behave during the breakdown of their lattices could help scientists develop more precise ways to control them. That control is particularly notable if these magnetic structures are to become useful components in future computer systems.

According to recent reports, the findings therefore offer more than a new way to observe an unusual magnetic phenomenon. They provide information that could help researchers overcome challenges involved in developing practical skyrmion-based technologies.

"The findings give us newly introduced insight into how these types of particles behave. This could therefore become key for the development of more energy-efficient computer technology in the future," said Sudbø.

Although substantial development is still needed before skyrmions can be used in everyday computing devices, the research highlights their potential for improving data storage, enabling new computing architectures, and supporting advances in quantum technology.

By learning to observe and manipulate these tiny magnetic vortices in real time, scientists are gaining capabilities that could eventually help reshape the design of computers.

"This could revolutionize the way we think about computers," concluded Sudbø.

Welcome EmbeddingGemma, Google's upcoming efficient embedding model

📅 04 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2735 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Today, Google releases EmbeddingGemma, a state-of-the-art multilingual embedding model perfect for on-device use cases.
  • Text embeddings have become the backbone of modern natural‑language applications, turning words, sentences, and documents into dense vectors that capture meaning, sentiment, and intent.
  • Industry observers note that building on this foundation, Google DeepMind’s EmbeddingGemma arrives as the newest, most capable small multilingual embedding model yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today, Google releases EmbeddingGemma, a state-of-the-art multilingual embedding model perfect for on-device use cases. Designed for speed and efficiency, the model features a compact size of 308M parameters and a 2K context window, unlocking upcoming possibilities for mobile RAG pipelines, agents, and more. EmbeddingGemma is trained to support over 100 languages and is the highest-ranking text-only multilingual embedding model under 500M on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) at the time of writing.

Text embeddings have become the backbone of modern natural‑language applications, turning words, sentences, and documents into dense vectors that capture meaning, sentiment, and intent. These vectors enable fast similarity search, clustering, classification, and retrieval across massive corpora, powering everything from recommendation engines and semantic search to retrieval-augmented generation and code‑search tools. Embedding models that calculate these embeddings are widely used, with well over 200 million monthly downloads on Hugging Face.

Industry observers note that building on this foundation, Google DeepMind’s EmbeddingGemma arrives as the newest, most capable small multilingual embedding model yet. With just 308M parameters, a 2k‑token context window, and support for over 100 languages, EmbeddingGemma delivers state‑of‑the‑art performance on the Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark (MMTEB) while staying under 200 MB of RAM when quantized.

The various design choices result in a very practical, open-source tool for computing high-quality multilingual embeddings on everyday devices.

In this blogpost, we describe the EmbeddingGemma architecture and training, and show you how to use the model with various frameworks like Sentence Transformers, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, txtai, Transformers.js, Text Embedding Inference, and ONNX.

Afterwards, we demonstrate how to finetune EmbeddingGemma on your domain for even stronger performance. In our example, we finetune EmbeddingGemma on the Medical Instruction and Retrieval Dataset (MIRIAD). The resulting model, sentence-transformers/embeddinggemma-300m-medical, achieves state-of-the-art performance on our task: retrieving passages of scientific medical papers in response to detailed medical questions. It even outperforms models twice as massive on this task.

EmbeddingGemma builds on the Gemma3 transformers backbone, but modified to use bi-directional attention instead of causal (one-way) attention. This means that earlier tokens in the sequence can attend to later tokens, effectively turning the architecture from a decoder into an encoder. Encoder models can outperform LLMs, which are decoders, on embedding tasks like retrieval (Weller et al., 2025). With this backbone, the model can process a sizable 2048 tokens at once, sufficient for typical retrieval inputs, especially given that larger inputs often result in information loss in the text embeddings.

Sources indicate that beyond the upcoming Gemma3-based encoder backbone, which produces token embeddings, a mean pooling layer converts these token embeddings into text embeddings. Lastly, two dense layers transform the text embeddings into their final form, a 768-dimensional vector.

Recent findings suggest that the EmbeddingGemma model has been trained with Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), allowing you to truncate the 768‑dimensional output to 512, 256, or 128 dimensions on demand. This results in faster downstream processing and lower memory and disk space utilization. See the Sentence Transformers usage for a snippet showing how to perform this truncation.

Industry observers note that the model has been trained using a carefully curated, multilingual corpus totalling approximately 320 billion tokens. The proprietary dataset is a blend of publicly available web text, code and technical documentation, and synthetic task‑specific examples. It has been filtered to avoid Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM), sensitive data, and low-quality or unsafe content.

EmbeddingGemma was benchmarked on the MMTEB (Multilingual, v2) and MTEB (English, v2) suites, which span a wide range of tasks, domains, and languages. Despite its modest 308M‑parameter size, the model consistently beats comparable baselines while keeping a very small memory footprint.

The results will be listed on the official MTEB Leaderboard. We exclude any model that has been trained on more than 20% of the MTEB data, to mitigate potential over‑fitting.

The demo can also be experienced in full screen.

Because google/embeddinggemma-300m was trained with MRL, the embeddings generated by this model can be truncated to lower dimensionalities without considerably hurting the evaluation performance. You can easily deploy EmbeddingGemma for both development and production using Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) version 1.8.1 or later.

If you run the Docker container with the cuda-1.8.1 tag, it includes support for multiple GPU architectures: Turing, Ampere, Ada Lovelace, and Hopper. For a lighter image tailored to just your GPU, you can instead use a specific tag such as turing-1.8.1, 1.8.1 and 86-1.8.1 (Ampere), 89-1.8.1 (Ada Lovelace), or hopper-1.8.1.

Once deployed, regardless of the device or runtime, you can leverage the /v1/embeddings endpoint based on the OpenAI Embeddings API Specification to generate embeddings.

Alternatively, you can also leverage the /embed endpoint from the Text Embeddings Inference Embeddings API, which supports the prompt_name parameter, meaning there’s no need to manually prepend the prompt to the inputs but select it via prompt_name instead.

Additionally, note that since google/embeddinggemma-300m was trained with Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), you can also leverage the dimensions parameter, on both /v1/embeddings and /embed, to truncate the embeddings to lower dimensionalities (512, 256, and 128) without hurting the evaluation performance.

You can also run the model directly with ONNX Runtime, making it highly portable and cross-platform compatible. The example below shows usage in Python, but the same approach can be applied in other languages (Java, C#, C++, etc.) as well.

It has been revealed that as with all models compatible with the Sentence Transformers library, EmbeddingGemma can be easily fine-tuned on your specific dataset. To showcase this, we'll be finetuning google/embeddinggemma-300m on the Medical Instruction and RetrIeval Dataset (MIRIAD) dataset, such that our finetuned model becomes particularly adept at finding passages up to 1000 tokens from scientific medical papers given detailed medical questions. These passages can be used as crucial context for a generative model to answer questions more effectively.

Below, you can explore each key component of the finetuning process using expandable tabs. Each tab contains the relevant code and a detailed explanation.

It has been revealed that this code loads the EmbeddingGemma model from Hugging Face, with optional model card metadata for documentation and sharing. The SentenceTransformer class loads the model weights and configuration, while the model_card_data argument attaches metadata useful for inclusion in the automatically generated model card.

This code loads the MIRIAD dataset, or rather, a copy that has been divided into train, eval, and test splits. Using a large, high-quality dataset ensures the model learns meaningful representations, while subsetting allows for faster experimentation. The load_dataset function fetches the dataset from Hugging Face Datasets, and the .select() method limits the number of samples for each split.

It has been revealed that this code defines the loss function for training, using Cached Multiple Negatives Ranking Loss (CMNRL). CMNRL is effective for retrieval tasks, as it uses in-batch negatives to efficiently train the model to distinguish between correct and incorrect pairs. The loss takes question-answer pairs and treats other answers in the batch as negatives, maximizing the distance between unrelated pairs in the embedding space. The mini_batch_size parameter controls the memory usage, but does not affect the training dynamics.

Industry observers note that it's recommended to use this loss with a large per_device_train_batch_size in SentenceTransformerTrainingArguments and a low mini_batch_size in CachedMultipleNegativesRankingLoss for a strong training signal with low memory usage. Additionally, the NO_DUPLICATES batch sampler is recommended to avoid accidental false negatives.

This code sets up all hyperparameters and configuration for training, evaluation, and logging. Proper training arguments are crucial for efficient, stable, and reproducible training. The arguments control batch sizes, learning rate, mixed precision, evaluation and saving frequency, and more. Notably, the prompts dictionary maps dataset columns to prompts used by the model to distinguish queries from documents.

This code sets up an evaluator for information retrieval, using queries and a corpus to measure model performance. Evaluation during training helps monitor progress and avoid overfitting. The evaluator computes retrieval metrics (NDCG, MRR, Recall, Precision, MAP, etc.) by checking if the model retrieves the correct passages for each query. It can be run before, during, and after training, and the results will be logged and incorporated in the automatically generated model card.

Note that this snippet in particular uses all (1k) evaluation questions against a corpus of all (1k) evaluation passages and 30k training passages, for a total of 31k documents. Evaluating only against evaluation passages is too simple for the model.

Additional time and compute investment would allow for even stronger results, such as hard negatives mining or training with more than 100k data pairs.

  • Here’s how to enter the Fortnite PlayStation Cup on your PlayStation, when each round takes place, and what you can win.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fortnite’s PlayStation Cup is back in November, giving PlayStation players a chance to compete for a share of $100,000 in cash prizes.

According to recent reports, the cup qualifiers start on November 23, with separate competitions for Battle Royale and Zero Build. Both are Solo events, so you can jump in without having to find a duo partner or put a squad together.

Here’s how to enter the Fortnite PlayStation Cup on your PlayStation, when each round takes place, and what you can win.

It has been revealed that before the Cup starts, make sure your PlayStation and Epic Games accounts are linked and that you’ve enabled two-factor authentication. Your Epic account needs to be in good standing and at least level 50, which you can check in the Career tab. You’ll also need to be at least 13 and meet the eligibility requirements for your country.

The Cup starts on Monday, November 23, with qualifiers for both Battle Royale and Zero Build. Top 80 players who advance in Zero Build will compete in the finals on Tuesday, November 24, while the Battle Royale finals take place on Wednesday, November 25.

This gives you just one day to book a spot in the finals, so you’ll have to rack up those wins as quickly as possible.

Each mode has $50,000 in prize money split across seven regions. In Europe, the top 50 finishers in each final earn cash, with $4,000 going to first place. North America Central also pays out to the top 50, with $2,500 for the winner.

In North America West, Brazil, the Middle East, Oceania, and Asia, the top 25 players in each final earn a cash prize, with $750 for first place.

A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, one of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it?
  • Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself.
  • The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, one of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.

Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or significantly disturbing the information it contains.

The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters. It was led by José Carlos Egues, a full professor at the São Carlos Institute of Physics at the University of São Paulo (IFSC-USP) in Brazil, and Yugui Yao of the School of Physics at the Beijing Institute of Technology in China. If experimentally confirmed, their method could simplify quantum computing by removing the need for extra qubits used in certain measurement techniques.

Why Measuring Quantum Information Is So Difficult.

Conventional computers store information in bits that have one of two values, 0 or 1. These values can be checked repeatedly without changing the information. Quantum computers work differently because their qubits can exist in superpositions, meaning they can combine the states 0 and 1 in ways that are not possible with conventional bits.

This unusual ability is central to the potential power of quantum computing. However, it also creates a major vulnerability. Quantum states can be disrupted by interactions with their surroundings, including the instruments scientists use to examine them.

Sources indicate that "In the conventional formulation of quantum mechanics, a projective measurement causes the system to assume one of the states associated with the measured quantity. Thus, if a qubit has been prepared in a certain superposition of 0 and 1, its direct measurement tends to destroy that superposition and, consequently, the information it contained," claims Egues.

To minimize this problem, physicists developed techniques known as "quantum nondemolition measurements," or QND. Many of these approaches use an additional quantum system called an ancilla. Rather than measuring the original qubit directly, researchers transfer information to the ancilla and measure that auxiliary system instead.

Recent findings suggest that the term "ancilla" comes from a Latin word meaning "slave" or "servant." In modern scientific usage, it describes something that performs a supporting function. Here, the ancilla acts as an intermediary, allowing researchers to obtain information while preserving the original qubit as much as possible.

According to recent reports, although effective, these procedures come with practical disadvantages. Scientists must prepare the auxiliary qubits, connect them to the qubits being studied, transfer information between them, and perform repeated measurements. These additional steps require time and equipment, and the complexity becomes increasingly significant as the number of qubits grows.

"Our strategy is different. Instead of transferring the information to an auxiliary qubit, we seek to obtain it from a signal produced by the qubit under study itself," says the researcher.

A Special Quantum Bit That Produces Its Own Signal.

According to recent reports, the proposed technique relies on the unusual properties of an Andreev qubit. Its name honors Soviet physicist Alexander Andreev (1939-2023), who identified a distinctive quantum process in 1964 that occurs where normal materials meet superconductors.

Recent findings suggest that superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity without electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. At the boundaries involving these materials, special quantum states known as "Andreev states" can form. In the system studied by the researchers, these states are confined to an extremely small region between two superconducting materials.

These quantum states can represent the basic values 0 and 1, along with superpositions of those values, making them suitable for storing quantum information.

According to recent reports, "In the system under consideration, this region is a quantum dot - that is, a nanoscale structure in which electrons are spatially confined - formed in an indium arsenide [InAs] nanowire connected to superconducting materials on both sides. It's in this environment that the states characterizing the Andreev qubit are formed," Egues explains.

The key to the fresh approach is an electrical phenomenon called a "supercurrent." Unlike the current flowing through ordinary electrical conductors, a supercurrent moves without resistance.

Sources indicate that the researchers found that when the Andreev qubit exists in a superposition, the supercurrent develops a component that oscillates over time. These fluctuations arise from quantum interference between the different states making up the superposition.

According to recent reports, crucially, the oscillations are not random. Their behavior contains information about the qubit's underlying quantum state, potentially allowing scientists to determine what that state is without directly measuring the qubit.

In a recent development, "It's precisely that property that we use to read the qubit. It's that supercurrent that lies at the heart of our proposal," the researcher points out.

How a Tiny Electrical Current Reveals Quantum Information.

To understand how the technique works, it helps to consider how physicists describe a qubit's state mathematically.

Sources indicate that one common representation is the "Bloch sphere," a geometric model in which every possible pure state of a single qubit corresponds to a point on the surface of a sphere. Two angles determine the location of that point.

The first angle describes how much each of the two basic states contributes to the superposition. The second describes their relative phase, which specifies how the quantum components are aligned with one another. Together, these two measurements provide the information needed to identify the qubit's state.

According to recent reports, according to the fresh research, both pieces of information can be extracted from the supercurrent. Its steady component and the size of its oscillations reveal the relative contributions of the two basic states. Meanwhile, the timing of the oscillations provides information about their phase relationship.

"Our study revealed that this information is encoded in the supercurrent itself. The supercurrent has a constant component and a fluctuating component. The value of the constant component and the amplitude of the oscillation reveal the proportion of each state (0 and 1) in the superposition, and the moment when that oscillation begins reveals the phase relationship between them. Thus, by measuring how the current varies over time, it's possible to reconstruct the initial state of the qubit," Egues explains.

This means the electrical current effectively carries a signature of the quantum information stored in the system. By observing how that signature changes over time, researchers could reconstruct the qubit's original state.

A Supercurrent That Oscillates Without Voltage.

Another surprising feature of the proposed system is that the electrical current can oscillate without an externally applied voltage.

Industry observers note that ordinarily, producing an oscillating supercurrent in this type of superconducting system requires a voltage. This familiar phenomenon is called the "AC Josephson effect.".

Recent findings suggest that the researchers predict something different in their Andreev qubit. Here, the current's oscillations arise naturally from the qubit's own quantum evolution. No outside voltage is required to generate them.

"Our system generates a supercurrent that varies over time like an alternating current but without voltage. It's the very evolution of the qubit's state that produces that oscillation," indicates Egues.

This behavior is important because it transforms quantum activity occurring on an extraordinarily small scale into a detectable electrical signal. The current provides a connection between the microscopic world of quantum states and the larger physical systems scientists can measure.

That connection is what makes the proposed reading technique possible.

Detecting Quantum States With an Extremely Sensitive Sensor.

The researchers envision placing the Andreev qubit inside a closed superconducting circuit, allowing its supercurrent to circulate continuously.

Next to the circuit would sit a SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device), a highly sensitive instrument capable of detecting extremely weak magnetic fields.

According to recent reports, whenever an electric current flows, it produces a magnetic field. Because the supercurrent in this system oscillates, the magnetic field it generates also changes over time.

The nearby SQUID could detect these tiny magnetic variations and use them to determine the behavior of the circulating current. Since the current contains information about the qubit's quantum state, the researchers could then reconstruct that state without measuring the qubit directly.

Egues compares the arrangement to two compasses that interact through a magnetic field.

"We can think of the qubit as one compass and the SQUID as another compass. The current in the circuit produces a magnetic field, and the SQUID 'senses' that field. Since the coupling between the two is very weak, the effect of the measuring instrument on the qubit tends to be very small.".

The weak interaction between the sensor and the qubit is especially crucial. It offers a way to gather information while minimizing the disturbance that normally accompanies quantum measurements.

Reading Quantum Information With Almost No Disturbance.

Sources indicate that in quantum physics, observing a system is not necessarily a harmless process. A measuring instrument interacts with whatever it is attempting to measure, and that interaction can change the system's behavior.

This fundamental difficulty puzzled the earliest researchers studying quantum mechanics. It remains an unavoidable feature of quantum measurements today.

The proposed technique does not eliminate this effect entirely. The SQUID still interacts with the circuit, creating a small amount of feedback that can influence the qubit. However, the team's simulations suggest that this disturbance can be reduced to a level so small that it becomes effectively negligible.

Sources indicate that "Our method doesn't eliminate the fundamental problem of quantum measurement. But it can approach the limit of a non-destructive readout and, at the same time, avoid the use of auxiliary qubits - the ancillas - employed in other non-destructive quantum measurement protocols," Egues notes.

According to recent reports, the approach could also remove another complication found in some existing techniques. Because researchers would not need to restore the qubit to its original state after every measurement, they could make repeated observations as the state changes.

This would allow scientists to follow the qubit's quantum evolution over time, rather than obtaining information only through separate measurement and reset cycles.

Simulations Achieve Up to 99.85% Accuracy.

To investigate whether the method could work outside ideal theoretical conditions, the researchers performed computer simulations designed to account for imperfections that would arise in real experiments.

Recent findings suggest that these calculations included measurement noise, as well as the small amount of feedback introduced by the detection coil. The goal was to determine whether the qubit's state could still be reconstructed accurately despite these disturbances.

The results were encouraging. Depending on the number of measurements used, the simulations produced accuracies of 99.52%, 99.81%, and 99.85%.

According to the researchers, these values fall within the standard thresholds used in quantum error correction schemes, which are designed to manage errors in quantum information processing.

The findings suggest that the method could provide highly accurate quantum state reconstruction without the additional complexity of auxiliary qubits.

However, the technique has not yet been demonstrated experimentally. The results come entirely from theoretical analysis and computer simulations, so researchers still need to establish whether a physical device can achieve comparable performance.

Could This Make Quantum Computers Simpler?

Despite the lack of experimental confirmation, the researchers emphasize that their proposal does not depend on technologies that have yet to be invented.

The calculations use realistic properties drawn from existing quantum systems, and SQUID sensors are already established tools for detecting exceptionally weak magnetic fields and electric currents.

What remains to be built is the specific arrangement of components required to implement the proposed measurement technique.

According to recent reports, "All the numbers we used are realistic. In principle, this can be achieved. In fact, we used parameters from existing systems in our calculations. What doesn't yet exist is that geometry, that setup that we proposed," he argues.

Sources indicate that this makes the approach different from theoretical concepts that cannot be realized until scientists develop entirely new materials or manufacturing techniques. In principle, the necessary components already exist, although assembling them into the proposed configuration and demonstrating the predicted behavior remain notable challenges.

The research offers two potentially significant advances.

From the standpoint of fundamental physics, it predicts that a qubit can produce an oscillating supercurrent resembling the AC Josephson effect, but without requiring an external voltage. Instead, the oscillations emerge from the qubit's own coherent quantum evolution.

From a technological perspective, the study reveals how those oscillations could serve as a measurable signature of the qubit's internal state. By analyzing the electrical current, researchers could recover quantum information while causing very little disturbance to the system.

In a recent development, if future experiments confirm these predictions, the method could make reading Andreev qubits substantially simpler. Eliminating auxiliary qubits and repeated resets could reduce the equipment and procedures needed to retrieve quantum information.

More fundamentally, the work points toward an intriguing possibility: information hidden in the microscopic quantum world may be accessible through an electrical current produced by the quantum system itself, offering a promising new way to observe delicate quantum states without destroying them.

#103650. I've never known a moment like this in video games

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1375 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

I've never known a moment like this in video games

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1375 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It was hard not to spend the first hour or so of Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day in a kind of stun-lock.
  • Industry observers note that the analogy falls apart pretty rapidly when you think about it: the heroism of writing a little article about a video game aside, the frenzy of this week has been a joy, not a horror.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's worth taking a moment just to actually, properly take stock of all the headlines from the past couple of days in terms of the sheer breadth and scale of its launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was hard not to spend the first hour or so of Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day in a kind of stun-lock. As far as video games editorial goes - which is not that far, in fairness; prepare for an over-flattering analogy - the effect was roughly the equivalent of Tom Hanks' experience, as his John H. Miller first set foot on Omaha beach. Tweets and reels whistled overhead, news leads stung the ears, exploding search terms blew apart some poor guides team ally on one side, while latest discoveries in the early game - made by the millions and millions of launch-day players all picking it apart at once - appeared by surprise like some flanking ambush on the other.

Industry observers note that the analogy falls apart pretty rapidly when you think about it: the heroism of writing a little article about a video game aside, the frenzy of this week has been a joy, not a horror. But the point is, I've been doing this job for over a decade now, paying attention to video games for another two beyond that, and I've truly never seen anything like this before. It has been totally overwhelming. And then I thought about that for a moment before realising that - duh - nobody has ever seen anything like this before. GTA 6 is the biggest entertainment release of all time, and it's not even remotely close.

Recent findings suggest that it's worth taking a moment just to actually, properly take stock of all the headlines from the past couple of days in terms of the sheer breadth and scale of its launch. Parent company Take Two revealed yesterday that GTA 6 sold 32.5m copies before it came out. By the end of its first day on sale, it had made a record-obliterating $3.79bn. By contrast, the once record-breaking GTA 5 made a once astounding $800m in the same period; the "opening" period of the largest film of all time, Avengers: Endgame, made $1.22bn, and that's totalling box office receipts across its release day until the end of the first Sunday after it.

It has been revealed that it has set multiple records for streaming, per StreamCharts, with 214.63m hours watched in its first two days - significantly more than the previous biggest game, Valorant, achieved with 150m hours in its entire launch week. It's garnered more watch time in those two days than Elden Ring, Hogwarts Legacy, and Cyberpunk 2077 achieved with their entire launch weeks combined. Its concurrent viewers peak so far - 6.38 million people - is nearly four times the previous record of 1.74m, again formerly held by Valorant.

It has been revealed that it crashed Reddit. More than 2 million UK and US Xbox players used the 'Latest Zealand trick' to play the game early, which is more than a third of that country's entire population. Internet exchange operator DE-CIX claimed its launch led to the highest amount of concurrent internet usage in history, at 33.03 terabits per second.

On top of all those raw numbers, it's also just felt utterly inescapable. I can't open Instagram, TikTok, BlueSky or X without being blasted with memes, viral clips of early discoveries, reactions, hot takes, feeble attempts at brand piggybacks, slightly wayward early-game tips from opportunist streamers who haven't escaped the first chapter, or makeup tutorials for looking like Lucia. I can't open my inbox without scrolling through reams of tenuous PR pitches for stories with barely the faintest connection to the game. I can't open my phone without messages from parents, friends or peers. Even the mainstream news - heaven forbid! - has gradually clocked onto this whole video games thing, this unknown artifact from the imaginary world of "online", maybe being a bit key. Dozens of my colleagues have been inundated with last-minute call-ups to provide an expert soundbite (they're so desperate they even got me on at one point).

According to recent reports, we'll have a lot more to say about this game in the coming days and weeks (with apologies to regulars who are already sick of it - counterprogramming starts this Monday!). It's the richest of texts, a near endless comedy clip generator, a total technical marvel and all the rest - you already know. But it felt worth it to just sit still for a moment, and take stock of what's happening here.

It has been revealed that this is the single biggest moment any piece of entertainment media has ever had. But more than that it's felt like a kind of party. The vibes in some corners are orgiastic, as streamers uncover spooky twists, outlandish reactivity, and easter eggs I'd never got close to in a hundred-odd hours with the thing - all of this pure dynamite for the audience. Given the budgets involved and the particularly unique blend of circumstances around it - the changing shape of video game funding; of how attention is monopolised; of how development may happen in the future and the sheer amount of time and subsequent anticipation built up since the previous entry - we will likely be waiting decades for another moment like it. If there's ever a moment like it again. Part of the sense of ecstasy going around comes, perhaps subconsciously, from the acknowledgment that in pure hype and attention terms, this might be as good as it ever gets.

Sources indicate that for the briefest time, the world belongs to video games. Rockstar and Take-Two's executives and shareholders will no doubt reap the greatest rewards from all this - all part of the great irony that makes this game's central premise all the more interesting. But I sincerely hope its developers - especially the 34 fired by the organization last year, now awaiting the outcome of their tribunal over alleged union-busting, and those who hope to form a union from the right now open vote - are able to feel a particular sense of pride.

Sources indicate that just as this launch has been unprecedented in its success, the last two or three years have been unprecedented in their grimness for video game workers across most of the world, certainly the once-dominat western part. If we're very lucky - and frankly, I have my doubts - this burst of attention and visible profitability might go some way to helping the industry claw its way back, perhaps via attracting, as a knock-on from all the latest-found attention, some kind of more sustainable investment. If we're not, and this is really the last behemoth, the last video game monument of its kind, the last rave before the police come raiding at dawn, at least we've gone out with one hell of a bang.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 - again, it's been said before now - is such a curious thing. A game of goofiness, self-awareness, prestige, pretentiousness, childish humour, astute commentary, ironic cultural criticism, surprising player expression and - above all of that - the most mind-boggling, brain-scrambling level of profoundly human craft. There's something kind of perfect about this.

It's a good thing, actually, that video games' greatest export is also its most contradictory. Video games are contradictory things in themselves. If the non-specialist media might still occasionally slip into treating video games like some kind of object from outer space, then we might as well put forward the best possible candidate for a capsule. It's the same way you'd think about it if you had to stick one thing in a vacuum-sealed box, to send out into the universe in an attempt to symbolise humanity: something that summarises close to all of it; that we're proud of; and crucially, that captures the spirit of it too.

Sources indicate that there are many more that might've put a more respectable foot forward - certainly that have a less chequered history, or maybe a more sophisticated, nuanced, or inventive use of the form. But there's really no better video game for exemplifying the full, chaotic range of the medium. It seems right, when you think about it, for GTA to be the one out there sitting under the spotlight, in the biggest moment this silly, serious artform might ever have.

"It stayed alive for so long" - Behind the wheel with the Last Riders saying goodbye to GTA Online, amidst GTA 6's world-changing launch
